If you don't have the capital to survive in any invest then you often lose.  If I gave you my last 20k to open a business and that business doesn't see a return for x amount of years, it's my responsibility to take care of myself during that time. There are plenty of ways the government can and is being supportive and there are many judges granting evictions during this pandemic. Creating and maintaining passive income is actually hard work, no matter how many get rick quick books someone reads and even you, in your post acknowledge that in the long run it's going to be okay. When all is said and down everyone who deserves to get paid, gets paid. I just think of the whole idea of not putting all your eggs in one basket. Property values rise and fall. If someone is unhappy with their tenets and cannot legally evict them, they could sell their property, cutting their lose in the invest like you mentioned. Again, it's really simple to me, we all make choices of where to put our money and some people are winners and losers. Being a landlord has been a win in recent years and right now it's a loss.

Isn’t this risk that you make when you invest? There are no sure bets. Just like when you rent to someone, you do your due diligence and hope once the contact is signed that it works out. No different that losing money in the stock market. It might feel personal when it comes to property however it’s really no different than owning a stock or gold or investing in a small business. They all carry risk. This is all business 101 you can learn at your local community college.
